title: Trait Emotional Intelligence in Italian Primary School Children: Psychometric Evaluation of the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire-Child Short Form and a Network Analysis of Socioemotional and School Functioning
abstract: Trait emotional intelligence (trait EI) is relevant to children’s emotional and social functioning, yet its psychometric organization and its position within the broader school context remain incompletely understood during middle childhood. The present research addressed these issues across two complementary studies with Italian primary school children. Study 1 (N = 668) examined the psychometric properties of the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire Child Short Form (TEIQue-CSF), including internal consistency, exploratory and confirmatory factor structure, measurement invariance, and percentile-based descriptive reference values. The general-plus-wording model improved fit relative to a one-factor model, but residual misfit and wording-related variance limit the interpretation of the total score. Measurement invariance was supported across sex. Exploratory analyses suggested partial metric invariance across grades; scalar invariance across grades was not established. Study 2 (N = 203), a secondary analysis of cross-sectional data, used network analysis to examine trait EI in relation to social intelligence, internalizing symptoms, academic performance, and classroom behavior. Trait EI showed high overall connectivity, with its strongest direct associations involving lower depressive symptoms and scholastic anxiety and higher Social Skills and Social Information Processing. Direct connections with academic performance were weak despite positive bivariate correlations. Additional factor-saturation indices supported a meaningful, although not dominant, general trait EI factor, while confirming substantial wording-related variance. Overall, the findings support use of the TEIQue-CSF total score as a broad summary index rather than as a strictly unidimensional measure, with additional caution required for comparisons across grades. In the cross-sectional network, trait EI was conditionally associated primarily with internalizing symptoms and self-reported social functioning.

journal.name: European Journal of Investigation in Health Psychology and Education
